RFC7950-6.5-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-09 after 180df07922 (Resolve returns *yang.Resolved, one Resolve per Loader; process, checkExtensions, checkPatterns, checkStructure still all run and join, refusals unchanged): cases unchanged. RFC 6.5: 'References to identifiers defined in external modules MUST be qualified with appropriate prefixes'. Prior judgement, still true: Re-judged 2026-10-09; unchanged cases. RFC7950-7.19-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-09 after 180df07922 (Resolve returns *yang.Resolved, one Resolve per Loader; process, checkExtensions, checkPatterns, checkStructure still all run and join, refusals unchanged): only the ModuleLoadAccepted tail changed. RFC 7.19: 'the substatements MUST be YANG statements, including extensions defined using "extension" statements.' The earlier finding that sources was keyed by file name no longer holds at HEAD: sourcedModules.texts is keyed by *yang.Module (Parse binds each module added by a parse to its text). Revert records on AddModuleFromText for the ModuleLoadAccepted/Refused tags are owed a re-record. Prior judgement, still true: Re-judged 2026-10-09 after 6c06cb43af/037cc25e29. Sentence 1: TestRFC7950ExtensionUsageSubstatementsAreYANGStatements refuses m:e "x" { bogus "y"; } against description and nested m:e twins. Sentence 2 (Section 14 rules) now whole: substatements are resolved against the embedded RFC ABNF (resolveProduction) and checked for argument grammar (config maybe, namespace not a URI, path a / ../a[), cardinality (two type, two description; one type + two must loads), required substatements and blocks (leaf without type, list without data-def, refine with no block) and context forms (deviate add/not-supported mixing, type-body alternatives, augment absolute vs descendant), each tagged test with a revert record on its producer. Independent probe 2026-10-09 of ~70 valid unusual forms under a usage (quoted/unquoted/single-quoted args, + concatenation, nested usages at depth, leafref require-instance, multiple leaf-list defaults, deviate add/replace/delete in full, if-feature expressions with extra whitespace, path predicates with WSP, IPv6/percent URIs, refine across comments/newlines/tabs/UTF-8/CRLF, nested module/submodule) all load; config TRUE, max-elements 0/007, fraction-digits 19, deref() path, refine x; via comment or concatenation, empty input/augment are refused. The ModuleLoadRefused/Accepted tags drive the extension DEFINITION (extension e { bogus }), governed by the Section 14 extension-stmt rule, a neighbouring rule; their claims state what the body checks but do not bear on this sentence.

RFC7950-7.6.5-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-12 (independent judge, fourth pass) after the review fixes to Fix A. Read at rfc/full/rfc7950.txt Section 7.6.5: "If "mandatory" is "true", the behavior of the constraint depends on the type of the leaf's closest ancestor node in the schema tree that is not a non-presence container (see Section 7.5.1): o If no such ancestor exists in the schema tree, the leaf MUST exist." Tested "the leaf MUST exist"; Gap "If no such ancestor exists in the schema tree"; Producer internal/component/config/validate_sections.go::ValidateCustomSections. ValidateCustomSections runs the full walk over validatedSections, mandatoryFailures over every other top-level section present in the config (Validator.Sections), and bgpMandatoryFailures over the whole bgp map, peer and group entries included, keeping only yang.ErrTypeMissing and dropping a failure only when EverySessionCarries answers true. isBGPGlobalPath is gone: the entry-path guard is now EverySessionCarries itself, which looks the first path segment (peer[p1]) up as a session field that no session holds, pinned by the untagged TestEverySessionCarriesNeverMatchesAnEntryPath. The change does not move this row's Tested scope: the leaves this bullet governs (bgp/router-id, bgp/session/asn/local) have no list entry in their path, walkTree's mandatoryPresent reads them from the bgp level of the same map whether or not peer and group are in it, and EverySessionCarries answers for them exactly as before. A mandatory node inside a peer or group entry has the list entry as its ancestor and belongs to RFC7950-7.6.5-3, which this verdict does not judge; TestMandatoryBGPPeerAndGroupEntriesAreWalked is untagged and earns this row nothing. Q1-Q4 for the Tested scope: TestRFC7950MandatoryRefusesBGPConfig drives LoadConfig on a bgp section with no peer, so no session can excuse the leaf, and asserts ErrCustomValidation with the exact path bgp/session/asn/local and its set command, then acceptance once the leaf is present; TestValidator_MandatoryField does the same for bgp/router-id; TestValidateTree_MandatoryMissing asserts ErrTypeMissing at bgp/router-id from the validator alone; TestRFC7950MandatoryWithNoQualifyingAncestor pins top/mid/need under an absent non-presence container with a test module, and no report once present. Each negative would go red if the producer stopped refusing; seven revert records replay (bgpMandatoryFailures at producer sha d5c4d88d6b9499a9, walkTree, missingMandatory, requireMandatoryUnderAbsent) and ./le rfc discriminate id RFC7950-7.6.5-1 lists no stale and no unproven entry. EverySessionCarries is added to the code map because both gap (b) and the entry-path guard now live in it. Gap, never counted conformant: (a) a whole top-level section absent from the config is not walked, owner ruling 6 (libyang LYD_VALIDATE_PRESENT); (b) bgp/router-id and bgp/session/asn/local absent globally while every session carries the value itself or from its group are counted present by EverySessionCarries, owner ruling "yes enforce". Whole requirement earns no credit.

RFC7950-7.6.5-3.note: Re-judged 2026-10-12, second pass (independent auditor) after 60a74fc04b, 600996fb77, 975428e1b3, 3f1bec74f0 and 84382339ce. Section 7.6.5: "Otherwise, the leaf MUST exist if the ancestor node exists in the data tree." The row's {partial} was removed in 60a74fc04b because the gap it declared (sections outside validatedSections) is closed: ValidateCustomSections now runs the full walk over validatedSections, mandatoryFailures over every other top-level section the compiled schema declares that is present in the config (Validator.Sections), and bgpMandatoryFailures over the bgp global level; LoadConfig, ze config validate, the web editor commit and the SSH editor commit (cli ConfigValidator.sectionErrors) all reach it. Negatives: TestRFC7950MandatoryOutsideValidatedSections has LoadConfig refuse a bfd profile whose auth presence container lacks type and secret, asserting ErrCustomValidation and both exact paths, in bfd, which the test asserts is outside validatedSections and inside Validator.Sections, so the refusal can only come from mandatoryFailures; TestRFC7950MandatoryRequiredWhenAncestorExists requires top/item[a]/inner/must and top/knob/sub/val when the list entry and presence container exist. Positives: the complete bfd profile loads; the leaves are not required when the ancestor is absent, and none is reported once supplied, so an over-eager walk goes red too. Records on mandatoryFailures, requireMandatoryUnderAbsent and walkTree. Population checked against today's schema: a scan of every conf module finds no mandatory node under bgp peer or group (bgpMandatoryFailures drops both lists before its walk) and no list or presence container inside a case holding one (walkTree does not descend into case data); every case-scoped mandatory leaf is RFC7950-7.6.5-2's population. Those two exclusions are latent and fail open for a future module (journal row, gate-excludes-part-of-its-population).

RFC7950-7.9.4-1.note: Judged 2026-10-12 (independent auditor). Section 7.9.4: "If \"mandatory\" is \"true\", at least one node from exactly one of the choice's case branches MUST exist." Tested "at least one node from"; Gap "exactly one of the choice's case branches"; Producer internal/component/config/yang/validator_mandatory.go::mandatoryPresent. Tested holds: TestMandatoryChoiceSatisfiedByACaseNode reports wrap/kind missing for a container with no node of any case (exact path), and accepts a node of one case and a node of a nested choice's case, so a lookup by the choice name alone, or one that ignores nested choices, goes red; records on mandatoryPresent (positive) and missingMandatory (negative). Real entry: walkTree's mandatory loop reaches it from ValidateCustomSections, so the static route choice action and the iface tunnel encapsulation choice kind are refused when empty. Gap holds: data with nodes from two cases is accepted at the first case node found and no other check compares the cases, so the exactly-one half is unmet; the conditional enforcement under a case or list ancestor in the following paragraph is a separate sentence. Whole requirement earns no credit; spec-config-yang-when-unique-choice.

Prior judgement, still true: Re-judged 2026-10-09; the earlier weak (min/max read as 0 and 2^64-1, and a one-part 5..1 tagged as parts out of order) is fixed. Non-negative: "-1..5" refused. Ascending: ModuleLoadRefused now drives "10..20 | 1..5", and TestRFC7950LengthPartsDisjointAndAscending refuses it and overlapping "1..5 | 3..8" (goyang coalesces both, so the refusal is checkStructure) against "0..5 | 10..20". min/max: TestRFC7950LengthMinMaxAreTheRestrictedTypeBounds refuses "min | 2" and "10 | max" over typedef length 2..10 against "min..4 | 6..max" and "min..max"; revert records on both structural tests. Probe 2026-10-09: touching "1..5 | 5..10" and "max | max" refused, adjacent "1..5 | 6..10" and "min | max" load; min/max follow a two-level typedef chain and a typedef with no length of its own; a union member's length is checked.

RFC7950-9.6.4.2-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-09 after 180df07922 (only the ModuleLoadAccepted tail changed; cases unchanged) over the goyang fork, now committed in 66e87707f5 (go.mod replace github.com/ze-software/goyang v1.6.4-0.20261009101552-a3cf525c4f98, upstream PR openconfig/goyang#317). The STACK now meets the sentence 'otherwise, the assigned value is one greater than the current highest enum value': vendored EnumType.Set sets last on the first assignment or any higher value (len(e.ToInt) == 0 || value > e.last), so SetNext after an explicit -5 yields -4, and Loader.Resolve (goyang Modules.Process) no longer refuses enumeration { enum p { value -5; } enum q; enum r { value 0; } }. Ze's own producer (assignEnumValues) is unchanged and its tags still discriminate: TestRFC7950EnumImplicitValueFollowsTheHighest pins -4 after -5, 11 after 10 then 3, if-feature counted (2), two typedef levels down, each refused twin differing only in the value; TestRFC7950EnumValueRangeAndUniqueness refuses with ErrEnumValue an implicit value past 2147483647 and an explicit repeat of the implicit -4. Both tags' claims state only what their bodies assert, and the edited comments now say only true things (goyang v1.6.3 history, Ze's own refusals). Still weak: the module that proves the stack fix is exercised only by TestGoyangNumbersAnEnumAfterANegativeValue, which carries no RFC requirement tag, and every tagged positive sidesteps the defect (uniqueness positive uses r value -3; the implicit positives restate q -4 in a restriction goyang builds afresh). Under goyang v1.6.3 every tagged unit stays green (TestGoyangNumbersAnEnumAfterANegativeValue still carries no tag and the uniqueness positive still uses r value -3), so dropping the replace at the next goyang bump (which the go.mod comment plans) reddens no tagged test. Owed to reach enforced: tag that module as a positive of this requirement (or change the uniqueness positive's r to value 0) and record its discrimination against the reverted Set.
